info.title: robo-fitting-room API
info.description: Versioned REST API exposed by `robo-fitting-room serve`. Handlers under `/api/v1/*` are stable; the unversioned `/api/*` aliases are deprecated and will be removed in the next release. Liveness / readiness probes sit at the root (`/healthz`, `/readyz`).

get.description:
One entry per `<asset_root>/urdf-fixture-collection/<id>/<id>.urdf`, sorted
by `id`; `urdf_rel` is that URDF's path relative to the asset root.

get.summary: List the floor plans (.obj, .dxf) in floor-plans/.
get.description:
The `*.obj` and `*.dxf` files directly in `<asset_root>/floor-plans/`
(extension in any case), sorted by name; `rel` is the file's path relative
to the asset root.

post.summary: Upload an OBJ floor plan into floor-plans/.
post.description:
A multipart upload: the `file` part is stored as
`<asset_root>/floor-plans/<filename>`, replacing a file of that name.
Returns `stored_path`, the stored file's path relative to the asset root,
and its size in `bytes`.

get.summary: List the dressed robots under urdf-dressed-robots/.
get.description:
One entry per `<asset_root>/urdf-dressed-robots/<id>/<id>.urdf`, sorted by
`id`; `urdf_rel` is that URDF's path relative to the asset root.

post.summary: Compose a manifest on disk into a USDA scene zip.
post.description:
Runs the compose pipeline against the manifest at `manifest_path` under
`asset_root`. The zip, holding the manifest and the composed
`<stem>.usda` stage, is streamed back as the response body with
Content-Type `application/zip` and the download name `<stem>.zip`. The
manifest is validated first: its errors return 400 `manifest_invalid`.

parameters.name: manifest_path
parameters.description:
Path under asset_root pointing at an existing manifest YAML, e.g.
`fitted-robots/scene.yaml`. Absolute paths and `..` segments are
rejected.

parameters.name: full_robots
parameters.description:
Keep the robots' full visual meshes. `false` (the default) drops them
and shows the collision hulls instead: a leaner zip, the same physics.
Fixtures always keep theirs.

parameters.name: full_tools
parameters.description:
Keep the tools' full visual meshes (default `true`); `false` shows only
their collision hulls. Independent of `full_robots`.

post.summary: Bundle a manifest's source URDFs and meshes into one zip.
post.description:
Builds the self-contained URDF-source bundle for the manifest at
`manifest_path` under `asset_root` and streams it back as
`application/zip`, with the download name `<stem>-urdf.zip`. The bundle
holds the scene YAML (rewritten to reference the URDFs by relative path)
plus every source URDF copied verbatim (each in its own folder with its
`meshes/` subtree) and the floor-plan OBJ when present. The manifest is
validated first: its errors return 400 `manifest_invalid`. This is a
SEPARATE artifact from `/compose`; the editor calls both when the user
opts in.

parameters.name: manifest_path
parameters.description:
Path under asset_root pointing at an existing manifest YAML, e.g.
`fitted-robots/scene.yaml`. Absolute paths and `..` segments are
rejected.

post.summary: Read a floor-plan OBJ's line segments.
post.description:
Body `{path, footprint_layers?}`. Parses the OBJ at the given relative
path through `floor_plan::load_floor_plan_with_footprint_layers` — the
manifest's `floor_plan.footprint_layers` split off as footprints, as
compose does — and returns the segment arrays as JSON. The editor's canvas
renders these directly. A DXF file isn't read (BL-22): a 400 says so.

Offset and scale are deliberately set to identity here — the editor
renders in DXF/OBJ-local coordinates and applies the user's
`cell_origin_dxf` pick on its own. The compose pipeline applies
the offset later.

400.description: Path resolution or OBJ parse error, or a DXF file

post.summary: Read a scene manifest's YAML text.
post.description:
Body `{path}`. Returns the raw YAML at `<asset_root>/<path>`, unchanged,
with Content-Type `application/x-yaml`. A missing file, or one that can't
be read as UTF-8 text, is 404 `manifest_not_found`.

post.summary: Write a scene manifest's YAML text.
post.description:
Body `{path, yaml}`. Path is resolved against `asset_root`; the YAML is
written verbatim, without validation, replacing any file there and
creating missing parent folders.

post.summary: List a URDF's actuated joints and their limits.
post.description:
Body `{path}`. Parses the URDF at `<asset_root>/<path>` and returns the
actuated (non-Fixed) joints in declaration order, with their limits in
degrees, or in metres for a prismatic joint. Used by the editor to render
one home-pose row per joint.

400.description: Path resolution or URDF parse error

post.summary: Validate a scene manifest given as YAML text.
post.description:
The body is the raw manifest YAML (`application/x-yaml` or `text/plain`);
its relative paths resolve against `<asset_root>/fitted-robots/`, as for a
manifest saved there. Returns `{ok, errors[], warnings[]?}`. The 200
response is used both for valid and invalid manifests; the `errors` array
is the success/fail signal, `warnings` (`scene::scene_warnings`, absent
when empty) what composes but probably not as meant. YAML that doesn't
parse, or a referenced file that can't be found, populates `errors` rather
than a 4xx.

get.summary: Liveness probe: always 200 with the crate version.
get.description:
Answers as soon as axum is accepting connections. The `version` field is
sourced from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` at compile time.

get.summary: Readiness probe: 200 once the asset root holds a URDF, else 503.
get.description:
200 when the asset root canonicalises and at least one `*.urdf` is
discoverable; 503 otherwise, with `ready: false` and the reasons in
`errors`. The walk is shallow (depth 4) so a misconfigured asset_root with
a giant filesystem doesn't stall the probe.

ComposeQuery.description:
Query parameters for compose: the CLI's `--full-robots` / `--full-tools`
flags, with the same defaults.

full_robots.description:
Keep the robots' full visual meshes. `false` (the default) drops them
and shows the collision hulls instead: a leaner zip, the same physics.
Fixtures always keep theirs.

full_tools.description:
Keep the tools' full visual meshes (default `true`); `false` shows only
their collision hulls. Independent of `full_robots`.

manifest_path.description:
Path under asset_root pointing at an existing manifest YAML, e.g.
`fitted-robots/scene.yaml`. Absolute paths and `..` segments are
rejected.

FloorPlanQuery.description:
A floor-plan request: the OBJ's path under the asset root and, optionally, the manifest's
`floor_plan.footprint_layers`, so the preview splits footprints as compose does.

footprint_layers.description:
The layers (or OBJ groups) drawn as footprints, by name, case-insensitively; layers named
like "footprint" are footprints anyway. Default: none.

path.description:
The OBJ's path relative to the asset root, e.g. `floor-plans/plan.obj`. Absolute paths
and `..` segments are rejected.

segments.description: Each segment is [[x, y, z], [x, y, z]].

HealthDto.description: Liveness probe response. `GET /healthz` always returns 200 with this.

lower_deg.description: A revolute or continuous joint's URDF limits, degrees.

lower_m.description: A prismatic joint's URDF limits, metres (its home value is in metres too).

path.description:
The file's path relative to the asset root, e.g. `urdf-dressed-robots/r1/r1.urdf` or
`fitted-robots/scene.yaml`. Absolute paths and `..` segments are rejected.

The manifest's path relative to the asset root, e.g. `fitted-robots/scene.yaml`; missing
parent folders are created. Absolute paths and `..` segments are rejected.

yaml.description: The manifest's YAML text, written verbatim (not validated).

UploadObjForm.description: The `multipart/form-data` fields of an OBJ floor-plan upload.

filename.description:
The name to store the file under, e.g. `plan.obj`; it must end in
`.obj` (any case). Only its last path component is kept, and every
character other than an ASCII letter, a digit, `.`, `_` or `-` becomes `_`.

UrdfBundleQuery.description:
Query parameters for the URDF-source bundle. The compose fidelity flags
(`full_robots`/`full_tools`) are USDA-only knobs and don't apply here, so
this endpoint takes just the manifest path.

manifest_path.description:
Path under asset_root pointing at an existing manifest YAML, e.g.
`fitted-robots/scene.yaml`. Absolute paths and `..` segments are
rejected.

warnings.description:
What composes, but probably not as the manifest means it (`scene_warnings`); these don't
fail validation. Absent when there are none.
